hypotheses.justification: Without this binder, instance synthesis still finds HasLimit F, so `limit.π F i` still elaborates. Mathlib provides `TopCat.topCat_hasLimitsOfSize [UnivLE.{v, u}] : HasLimitsOfSize.{w, v} TopCat.{u}` (Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Basic.lean:173). The needed `UnivLE.{v, max v u}` comes from `univLE_of_max` plus `UnivLE.self` (Mathlib/Basic/UnivLE.lean:67,74). Since `J : Type v` is a SmallCategory, this gives HasLimitsOfShape J TopCat.{max v u} and hence HasLimit F. Mathlib already relies on this: `TopCat.piIsoPi {ι : Type v} (α : ι → TopCat.{max v u})` uses `∏ᶜ α` and `limit.isLimit _` with no HasLimit assumption. The library itself also builds this limit with `TopCat.limitConeIsLimit F` (line 278). The theorem stays true because the limit always exists here. The proof is unchanged: `limitCylinder_subset_iff_eventually F i hX hmap (limit.cone F) (limit.isLimit F) U V hUopen hUcompact hVopen` works for any limit cone, now taken from the global instance. Not compiled, since Lean could not be run; this rests on reading the instance sources.
